rules.title: Frame capture is diagnostic until validation completes
rules.observed: Atlas can attach process-bound PresentMon FPS and frame-time evidence when ETW permission is available. This path has not yet passed the full anti-cheat and overhead gate.
rules.why_it_matters: Average FPS cannot prove smoothness or input responsiveness. Atlas will not substitute an inaccurate counter.
rules.expected_benefit: Diagnostic sessions can already correlate long frames with GPU, CPU, memory, thermal, storage, and background activity.
rules.tradeoff: Atlas shows the measured values but will not use them for before-and-after improvement verdicts until the validation matrix passes.
rules.verification: The session must contain usable dominant-swap-chain frame samples. Comparison remains locked until the ETW validation matrix passes.

rules.title: The active desktop refresh rate is low for competitive play
rules.observed: Windows reports the primary desktop below 100 Hz.
rules.why_it_matters: A game cannot present new frames to this display faster than its active scan-out rate, and a mistaken 60 Hz mode can make a fast PC feel delayed.
rules.expected_benefit: Using the monitor's intended refresh rate can improve motion clarity and reduce display-side delay.
rules.tradeoff: Higher refresh can increase laptop power use and may require a different cable, port, or resolution.
rules.restart_requirement: The game must be restarted after a display-mode change.
rules.rollback: Choose the previous Windows display mode; Windows also provides timed display reversion.
rules.verification: Atlas rereads the active desktop refresh rate after the change.

rules.title: The PC is running on battery power
rules.observed: Windows reports that external power is not connected.
rules.why_it_matters: Gaming laptops commonly reduce sustained CPU and GPU power on battery, which can lower frame-rate consistency.
rules.expected_benefit: Connecting the correct charger can restore the laptop's intended sustained performance envelope.
rules.tradeoff: Higher performance increases heat, fan noise, and power use.
rules.restart_requirement: None; retest after power state stabilizes.
rules.verification: Atlas confirms AC power and compares a new session.

rules.title: Windows 11 can use the modern windowed presentation path
rules.observed: This PC is running a supported Windows 11 build.
rules.why_it_matters: Compatible DirectX 10 and 11 games can move from the legacy blt path to flip model, which supports lower frame latency and modern display features.
rules.expected_benefit: Potentially lower windowed or borderless presentation latency on compatible games.
rules.tradeoff: Compatibility is game-specific, so this remains an observed setting and an isolated experiment rather than a universal fix.
rules.rollback: Restore the previous per-game graphics preference.
rules.verification: Compare equivalent sessions and keep only a result outside the noise band.

rules.title: Use the game's native latency control when supported
rules.observed: Counter-Strike 2 is installed. Atlas has not read a recognized game configuration yet, so the current Reflex state is unknown.
rules.why_it_matters: Native Reflex coordinates the game's CPU and GPU submission path and is most useful when GPU utilization is high.
rules.expected_benefit: Lower render-queue latency on compatible NVIDIA hardware, especially in GPU-bound moments.
rules.tradeoff: Enabled + Boost can increase power use and may slightly reduce frame rate.
rules.restart_requirement: None for the in-game setting; measure a fresh session.
rules.rollback: Restore the previous in-game Reflex value.
rules.verification: Confirm the in-game value, then compare matched sessions.

rules.title: Confirm the native latency setting
rules.observed: VALORANT is installed, but its current latency and multithreaded-rendering settings were not read by a recognized adapter.
rules.why_it_matters: The game's native latency path is preferable to a driver override when supported.
rules.expected_benefit: Lower PC latency on compatible hardware without disabling Vanguard or Windows security.
rules.tradeoff: Boost modes can use more power; unsupported fallbacks must be tested separately.
rules.restart_requirement: Measure a fresh match after changing the setting.
rules.verification: Use comparable sessions and keep Vanguard/security state unchanged.

sources.title: NVIDIA Reflex: Apex Legends, VALORANT, Fortnite and CS2

rules.title: Choose the renderer with a controlled comparison
rules.observed: Fortnite is installed, but Atlas has not verified whether Performance mode or DirectX 12 is the better fit for this hardware.
rules.why_it_matters: Renderer choice changes shader behavior, CPU overhead, image quality, and feature availability; a universal answer is unreliable.
rules.expected_benefit: A renderer matched to the PC can improve sustained frame pacing.
rules.tradeoff: The first runs after a renderer change can include shader warm-up. Competitive profiles keep frame generation off because generated frames do not replace input samples.
rules.restart_requirement: Restart Fortnite and exclude shader warm-up from comparison.
rules.rollback: Restore the previous renderer and frame-generation values from the checksummed backup.
rules.verification: Compare at least three matched sessions after warm-up.

rules.title: Set a cap from measured sustainability, not a copied number
rules.observed: Apex Legends is installed, but Atlas does not yet have validated frame-time sessions for this PC.
rules.why_it_matters: A cap the system can hold can reduce oscillation and GPU saturation; the correct value depends on this hardware, display, map, and settings.
rules.expected_benefit: More consistent pacing and better latency control when the cap leaves useful GPU headroom.
rules.tradeoff: A lower cap sacrifices peak FPS. Texture streaming budget also needs to stay within measured VRAM headroom.
rules.rollback: Restore the prior cap and texture budget.
rules.verification: Use three comparable sessions and median frame-time evidence.

rules.title: Prefer Overwatch's native latency control
rules.observed: Overwatch is installed, but the current Reflex or Reduce Buffering state has not been verified.
rules.why_it_matters: Native latency controls can reduce the render queue while preserving the game's security and input path.
rules.expected_benefit: Lower PC latency on supported hardware.
rules.tradeoff: Renderer changes and High Precision Mouse Input should be isolated as separate experiments.
rules.restart_requirement: Measure a fresh session after the change.
rules.verification: Confirm the in-game diagnostic state and compare matched sessions.

rules.title: Separate rendering delay from connection delay
rules.observed: Rocket League is installed, but Atlas cannot read the game's Performance or Network graph state from a recognized configuration adapter yet.
rules.why_it_matters: Rocket League exposes separate Frame, Game, Render, GPU, packet-loss, latency, and input-buffer signals. They help distinguish a slow frame on this PC from an unstable route or server symptom instead of calling every problem lag.
rules.expected_benefit: Clearer evidence when a stutter, delayed input, rubber-banding, or inconsistent match occurs.
rules.tradeoff: The in-game graph uses some screen space and still needs to be correlated with an Atlas session before drawing a conclusion.
rules.restart_requirement: None; enable the graph from Settings > Interface before a measured session.
rules.rollback: Set Performance Graphs back to None and leave Connection Quality Indicators at the previous value.
rules.verification: Mark the incident in Atlas and compare its timestamp with Rocket League's Frame, Game, Render, GPU, loss, latency, and input-buffer readings.

rules.title: Reduce only the graphics work that is missing the frame budget
rules.observed: Rocket League is installed, but its current video settings and sustainable frame-time budget have not been verified by Atlas.
rules.why_it_matters: Lower render quality can help when GPU time is late, while lowering visuals cannot fix a network-loss or game-thread problem. Atlas should identify the late lane before suggesting a quality tradeoff.
rules.expected_benefit: A controlled performance preset test can improve frame consistency when the GPU is the measured limit.
rules.tradeoff: Performance-oriented anti-aliasing, render, texture, world, and particle settings reduce image quality. A copied preset may provide no benefit when the GPU is not the bottleneck.
rules.restart_requirement: Start a fresh comparable session after changing one group of settings.
rules.rollback: Restore the prior in-game video values recorded before the experiment.
rules.verification: Compare matched sessions and keep the change only when the effect is outside the 5% noise band; three comparable sessions are required for a verified verdict.
